title: Same-run composite FKs and per-version vocabulary FKs at run scale, with the s6.volume rerun on 18/corpus
question: At D3 §11's run scale (10^5 observations, 10^4-10^5 claims), what do the target model's same-run composite FKs (UNIQUE (run_id, id) targets; kb.claim_ref and kb.claim_entity_ref (run_id, ...) REFERENCES kb.claim/kb.entity (run_id, id); kb.claim.attribution_entity_id) and per-version vocabulary FKs ((schema_version_id, predicate) -> meta.schema_slot for INV-03; (schema_version_id, kind) -> meta.statement_kind) cost on binary COPY and run deletion on 18/corpus, and does the s6.volume result hold on the dedicated cluster?
answers: INV-03 and INV-08 enforcement placement (model-and-projections §3.4, foundations §3.8)
method: A base database cloned from cs_template with S6's applied DDL and S6-B's row load (copies in code/q4_s6, patched only for the cluster, paths and no SET ROLE), cloned afresh for every repetition in its own process. (a) S6's s6e_volume.py unchanged, 5 repetitions. (b) A scratch TM §6 addendum over S6's DDL in three placements (t_none: columns, edge tables and overlay indexes, no same-run or vocabulary FK, edges deleted by run_id; t_samerun: plus UNIQUE (run_id, id) and five cascading composite FKs; t_all: plus the two vocabulary FKs), writing S6's tasks and observations, 2,500 Statement entities, claims with the new columns, 1 claim_ref and 4 claim_entity_ref rows per claim; 5 repetitions per placement at 2x10^4 claims (order rotated), 3 of t_none and t_all at 10^5 claims; rolled-back negative inserts; the bulk-writer equivalent check timed in Python. psycopg 3.3.6 binary COPY with Copy.set_types, client wall clock. PostgreSQL 18.6 on 18/corpus (ops/postgresql/corpus.conf: shared_buffers 8GB, work_mem 64MB, maintenance_work_mem 8GB, synchronous_commit off, fsync on, io_uring, jit off, random_page_cost 1.1); AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D (16C/32T), 188 GiB, Linux 7.0.0-38; Python 3.14.10; another session's multiprocess job ran concurrently (1-minute load average 5-13, recorded per run). Databases p0q_fk* dropped afterwards.

agents.separation: coordinator brief; wrote only code/q4_*, code/q5_*, code/q4_s6/, results/q4/, results/q5/, records/p0q.fk-cost.json, records/p0q.pool-roundtrip.json and the README's Q-4 and Q-5 sections

conclusion: On 18/corpus the s6.volume figures hold (binary COPY is client-bound: 100,000 observations in about 1.19 s, 20,000 claims in 0.23 s; deletion 0.30 s), with two query plans changed to index paths. Same-run composite and per-version vocabulary FKs cost about +0.58 s on a 2x10^4-claim run's materialized writes (+78%; +28% of the whole load) and +2.9 s at 10^5 claims, linear in rows at about 2.4 µs per FK probe, nearly all on the edge rows; deletion +0.2 s and +1.0 s. They refuse cross-run and unknown-vocabulary rows; the bulk-writer placement would save that time but needs its own check (4-21 ms) and edge deletion and guards only its own writes. Input to P0-M-2/P0-F-4: FK enforcement is acceptable at this scale; declare INV-03 and INV-08 as FKs, with a referencing-side index for every composite FK no existing index leads with (at least kb.claim (run_id, attribution_entity_id), whose absence made deletion take 9.3 s).
